acme.caHint: Must match the CA recorded on the certificate exactly — renewal looks the account up by CA, and a mismatch is the same as having none.
acme.desc: The account used for automatic certificate renewal. Without one, the renewal task fails for every certificate.
acme.emailHint: The CA sends expiry and revocation notices here, so use an address that is actually monitored.
acme.emptyBody: The automatic renewal task fails for every certificate with "no matching ACME account". That failure is only visible in the scheduled task's run history — the certificate list itself looks fine, until they actually expire.
acme.title: ACME accounts

action.downloadHint: Download the certificate bundle (zip: cert + private key + chain). Contains a private key; the download is audited

apply.accountHint: Renewal looks up the account by CA, so the certificate's CA follows the account you pick
apply.challengeHint: dns-01 supports wildcards; http-01 requires the domain to be reachable from the internet
apply.cnHint: For a wildcard use *.example.com, which requires dns-01
apply.desc: Requests from the CA over ACME. Issuance is asynchronous; watch the status in the list.
apply.domainHint: Linking shows in the graph which domain this certificate protects

noAccount.noKey: The existing ACME accounts have no account key, so they are inert. Add the key before requesting.
noAccount.none: There is no ACME account yet. Create one via "ACME accounts" on this page — without it, auto-renewal fails for every certificate.
noAccount.title: Cannot request certificates yet

apply.quotaNote: CAs rate-limit issuance (Let's Encrypt: 5 per week per domain set). Requests and renewals consume quota, failures included — which is why neither is retried automatically.
apply.sansHint: One per line. No need to repeat the CN
apply.stagingHint: Staging is for rehearsing the flow and does not consume production quota
apply.stagingWarn: ⚠️ Staging certificates are not trusted by browsers. Use them to rehearse the flow only; never deploy them.
apply.title: Request certificate

caveat.title: A whole column of data is missing from this list

notRevoke.body: Only the CMDB record is removed. The issued certificate remains trusted until it expires — if the private key leaked, revoke it at the CA.
notRevoke.title: This is not a revocation

dnsReady.hint: Add the TXT record below at your DNS provider, wait for it to propagate, then continue.

noChallenge.body: Status {{status}}, challenge {{challenge}}. Either validation has not started, or this certificate does not use dns-01.
noChallenge.title: No DNS challenge pending

dnsReady.noChallengeBlock: No challenge record yet — releasing now would fail
dnsReady.title: Release DNS validation
dnsReady.tooEarlyWarn: ⚠️ Continuing before the TXT record propagates fails validation and burns one CA quota unit. Confirm with dig first.

empty.filtered: No certificates match the current filters. Try widening them.
empty.noSource:
This page lists certificates we manage (issued via ACME or registered by hand) — there really are none.
Certificates actually serving traffic are not here; they are under "Expiry inspection" in this page's toolbar (probed from the domain and CDN side, several hundred of them).
To get data here, issue via ACME or register one by hand under "Domains & ingress → Certificates".
empty.title: No certificates

inspect.desc: Expiry dates probed from port 443, plus what the inventory records. Note: this is NOT the Runtime / Inspection page — that one checks scheduled-task health.
inspect.internalNote: {{count}} more resolve to internal addresses — a public prober cannot reach them by definition, so they do not count as probe failures.
inspect.probeTitle: The expiry dates below are incomplete
inspect.title: Certificate expiry inspection

probe.neverTaskDisabled: {{never}} certificates have never been probed: the scheduled job "Certificate expiry check (443)" is disabled and has never run. Their expiry dates are unknown — not absent — which means expiry warnings are not working at all right now. Go to Operations → Scheduled tasks, find that job, enable it and run it once.
probe.neverTaskNotRun: {{never}} certificates have never been probed: the job "Certificate expiry check (443)" is enabled but has never executed. Go to Operations → Scheduled tasks, find that row and use "Run now" to verify it.
probe.neverUnknownTask: {{never}} certificates have never been probed. Their expiry dates are unknown — which is not the same as having no expiry date.
probe.partialSinceLastRun: {{never}} certificates have no probe result even though the job last ran at {{lastRun}} — so those targets were not covered by that run, or the results were not written back.
probe.someFailed: {{failed}} probes failed, so their expiry dates are unavailable. See the "Result" column for why (targets resolving to internal addresses do not count as failures).
